newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Suffolk lawmakers OK LILCO referendum - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Suffolk lawmakers OK LILCO referendum - paper.

text.p: Lawmakers in Suffolk County, N.Y., unamimously voted to hold a November referendum on Gov. George Pataki's plan to partly take over the Long Island Lighting Co, the New York Times reported Wednesday.
Passage of the referendum would require Suffolk officials to oppose the plan by all means available, including legal action, according to the Times.
That would be a major embarrassment to the Republican governor, who got critical support from Suffolk in the 1994 gubernatorial race.

Pataki, who proposed the partial takeover partly at the request of Suffolk Republicans, has promised it will cut by 17 percent electricity rates for residents in Suffolk County and neighboring Nassau County. Suffolk also would get another boon -- a 50 percent reduction in a $1.2 billion debt it owes LILCO for overtaxing its shuttered Shoreham nuclear plant.
The New York Times said Nassau officials were baffled by the Suffolk County legislature's decision to put the referendum on the ballot.

The Suffolk County Executive, Robert Gaffney, is a long-time critic of LILCO and a strong support of Pataki's plan. While Gaffney cleared the way to put the measure on the ballot in November, the paper said he predicted Suffolk County's voters would support Pataki's plan to sell nearly $7.3 billion of bonds to finance the transaction.

Under the governor's proposal, a state agency, Long Island Power Authority, would buy assets from LILCO and Brooklyn Union Gas. Shareholders of the two companies in early August approved a merger plan, as well as the partial state takeover of LILCO.
